-The doctrine an integration must follow lives in three always-on rules plus one full checklist — **read the checklist before any non-trivial integration edit:**

+**Read [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](references/integration-patterns.md) before any non-trivial integration edit.** It is the full pass/fail checklist the reviewer enforces. These rules load automatically when you touch integration files:

-- [`.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md`](.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md) — faithfully represent the source API: loud failures > quiet workarounds, spec-is-canonical, root-cause-first before any escape hatch, the shallow-fix family, `IntegrationNotImplemented` vs `None`, date / `trackstar_tags` invariants.

-- [`.claude/rules/write-safety.md`](.claude/rules/write-safety.md) — `allow_writes()` / `test_account()`, never write to vendor prod (HTTP method isn't the gate; the operation's effect on vendor data is).
-- [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](.claude/rules/integration-testing.md) — the live `TestX` class is the only test surface; never modify a failing test to pass.

-- [`.claude/references/integration-patterns.md`](.claude/references/integration-patterns.md) — the full pass/fail checklist subagents enforce (format output shape, data access, file structure + ordering, resource scope + dependency chains, write safety, code style). The source of truth, covering cases the rules summarize.

+- [`.claude/rules/integration-fidelity.md`](rules/integration-fidelity.md): represent the source API faithfully. Fail loudly instead of working around quietly, find the root cause first, `IntegrationNotImplemented` vs `None`, date and `trackstar_tags` rules.

+- [`.claude/rules/write-safety.md`](rules/write-safety.md): `allow_writes()` / `test_account()`. Never write to a vendor's production account; what matters is the effect on vendor data, not the HTTP method.
+- [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](rules/integration-testing.md): the live `TestX` class is the only test surface. Never change a failing test to make it pass.
## Testing

-`yarn test` with filters is the only test entry point — **never** `python -m pytest` / raw `pytest`; for ad-hoc Python use `uv run python3`, never raw `python3` (both in [`.claude/rules/code-style.md`](.claude/rules/code-style.md); flags in the `run-scripts` skill). Integration test rules: [`.claude/rules/integration-testing.md`](.claude/rules/integration-testing.md).
-## Available Commands
-- `/catchup` - review branch changes
-- `/debug-report` - investigate customer issues
-- `/generate-support-email` - draft email to WMS/API vendor
-- `/claudish` - opt in to (or pause, restyle, or inspect) the plain-language rewrite of assistant messages on your own screen; off for everyone until `/claudish on` (see `.claude/hooks/README.md`)
-## Available Skills

-- **plan-integration** - autonomously build a NEW integration end-to-end: no human gates, parallel resource-cluster fan-out in worktrees, park-and-continue on non-convergence, PR opened ready for review + Slack/Linear status; humans review via PR comments (`/plan-integration <ticket-url-or-paste>`, or put the `bot-build` label on a Linear issue)

-- **iterate-integration** - run the writer+reviewer loop on existing integration code for fix-type work (failing tests, customer-issue fixes, regression patches) (`/iterate-integration "<task>" [--ship]`)

-- **fix-tests** - triage failing tests from the daily CI report (or any pytest output) — integration (`test/integrations`) and non-integration (api/celery/lambda/utils/transports) — classify the root cause, and ship fixes as a draft PR per sweep (separate sweeps per family, since CI scopes them differently), never validation-weakening shortcuts (`/fix-tests <slack-link | actions-run | pasted failures | integration>`)

-- **review-dependabot-prs** - vet the open Dependabot bumps and fold them into one of the existing Dependabot PRs: triage each package into a blast-radius class (silent-runtime / trust-anchor / contract / infrastructure / leaf), diff the package source between the two versions rather than trusting release notes, set versions in `pyproject.toml` and regenerate `uv.lock`, then push the lot onto the host PR's branch and rewrite its body with per-package evidence and the superseded PRs named. Never merges (`/review-dependabot-prs`)

-- **integration-pr** - create or refresh a pokedex integration PR (body + field-mapping comment). No arg = create from current branch; positional `<pr>` = refresh existing PR via detect-and-patch (`/integration-pr [<pr-url-or-number>]`)

-- **wrap-integration** - finalize an integration build and open its PR: coverage check, support-email draft, test sweep, field-mapping skeleton, holistic whole-file review loop, then the PR via `/integration-pr` + Linear comment. Its mechanics are reused by reference inside `/plan-integration` (compose + finalize); run it standalone on a hand-built integration (`/wrap-integration`)

-- **installation-guide** - create the customer-facing Notion installation guide (Installation Guides page, trackstarhq workspace) and set `installation_guide_url` in the manifest; the manifest test asserts the guide is publicly readable and non-empty. Invoked during scaffolding, or standalone to backfill placeholder guides (`/installation-guide <integration-name>`)

-- **knowledge-base** - read Greptile's synthesized architecture docs for any trackstarhq repo (including siblings not checked out here) to get oriented before reading code, and see the custom-context rules Greptile reviews PRs against; verifies Greptile is configured first
-- **scrape-docs** - scrape API documentation into LLM-optimized markdown
-- **validate-api** - test API auth and collect samples before implementation
-- **run-scripts** - reference for crawl, test, curl, serve, generate commands
-- **review-code** - code review checklist for production readiness

-- **se-investigate** - SE front door for a Pylon ticket: triage → check if we've answered it before (Slack/past tickets) → run `investigate` → post internal note. Runs unattended via a local poller (`/se-investigate <pylon-issue-id>`)

-- **agent-pylon-investigate** - unattended cloud-routine variant of `se-investigate`: fired per new ticket by a Pylon webhook → routine, self-dedups, wraps `investigate`, posts a Pylon internal note + opens a draft PR for a clear fix to the reported bug; unrelated bugs found along the way go in the note, never a PR, and become at most one Linear card per ticket (`/agent-pylon-investigate <pylon-issue-id>`)

-- **distill** - weekly consolidation pass over `.claude/` markdown, run as a scheduled routine on the bot account: compacts api-summary files to current API behavior and promotes patterns human reviewers taught on PRs into gotchas / rules / CLAUDE.md — or into the producing skill's own instructions when a review corrected skill-dictated behavior. Markdown only; single draft PR per run (`/distill [--lookback <days>]`)

-- **investigate** - canonical investigation skill for any trackstar issue (missing/wrong data, webhooks, sync delays, stale schedules, crawl errors, credentials); composes query-datadog + per-issue workflows
-- **update-crawl-frequency** - update crawl frequencies on connections to change sync intervals
-- **bulk-resync** - query DynamoDB for connections by org + integration, populate and run bulk resync

-- **create-linear-issue** - the one surface that creates a Linear issue, so every flow files cards the same way. Two modes: compose from a freeform ask (pick the Type label + integration/customer label, write a short human body), or file a caller-supplied spec from an automated skill, keeping its title, labels and fenced blocks but trimming the prose to the body ceiling and landing it in **Robot Draft** rather than the shared backlog. Always reads the live labels and statuses, never invents a label. Out of scope: editing/closing issues (`/create-linear-issue "<ask>" [priority=…] [assignee=…] [labels=…] [project=…]`)

-- **claudish-output** - rewrite the prose of an outgoing text (PR title or body, Linear card, Slack or email reply) into plain English with the claudish-to-english prompts and the house rules in `.claude/rules/communications.md`; Claude Haiku does it through the session's own Claude Code binary, on a laptop or in a cloud session alike, with the installed plugin's local model as an opt-in alternative; templates, machine-read lines, fenced blocks and links pass through untouched (`/claudish-output`, or "claudish to english")
-- **worktree** - manage git worktrees for feature branches (`/worktree add|remove branch-name`)
-## Available Subagents
-Spawn with `Agent({subagent_type: ..., ...})`. Mostly used by `/plan-integration`, but the reviewer and api-validator are useful ad-hoc.

-- **integration-reviewer** — reviews one file or diff against `references/integration-patterns.md`; runs targeted `yarn test`; no edit access. Use when debugging an integration, investigating a customer issue, or pre-PR.
-- **integration-api-validator** — re-characterize an API and refresh exemplar guidance when a vendor's API changes.
-- **integration-function-writer** — implement one coherent unit; mainly orchestrated, ad-hoc only for narrow single-method adds.
-## Context Management
-- for multi-phase work, document progress to a plan and use `/clear` between phases
-- read knowledge / reference files on-demand, don't preload
-- use Planning Mode for new integration work or when scope is unclear
-## Working Directories
-- plans → `.claude/plans/` (gitignored)
-- temp scripts → `.claude/tmp/` (gitignored)

-- scraped docs → `.claude/references/{integration}/` — **partly committed**: `api-summary.md` and text notes are committed (they're the decisive log a PR is reviewed against); the bulky and binary source material is not (`*.xsd`, `*.pdf`, `openapi*.json`, `*.postman_collection.json`, `samples/`, `sample_*.json`, `spec_extract/`). `git check-ignore -v <path>` settles any specific file.
+`yarn test` with filters is the only way to run tests. Never `python -m pytest` or raw `pytest`. For ad-hoc Python use `uv run python3`, never raw `python3`. Flags are in the `run-scripts` skill.
+## Working
+- Git rules: [`.claude/rules/git-workflow.md`](rules/git-workflow.md). PR rules: [`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md`](rules/pull-requests.md).
+- For multi-phase work, keep progress in a plan and `/clear` between phases. Use plan mode for new integration work or unclear scope.
+- Read knowledge and reference files when you need them, not up front.
+- Plans go in `.claude/plans/`, temp scripts in `.claude/tmp/` (both gitignored).

+- Scraped docs go in `.claude/references/{integration}/`. `api-summary.md` and text notes are committed; bulky or binary sources are not (`*.xsd`, `*.pdf`, `openapi*.json`, `*.postman_collection.json`, `samples/`, `sample_*.json`, `spec_extract/`). `git check-ignore -v <path>` settles a specific file.
-# Agents Directory
+# Agents
-Holds the subagents that drive `/plan-integration`. They can also be spawned ad-hoc — particularly the reviewer for debugging or pre-PR checks.
+The subagents that `/plan-integration` runs. You can also spawn them directly, most often the reviewer, for debugging or a pre-PR check.
-| Agent | Role | Ad-hoc use? |
+| Agent | Role | Ad-hoc use |

-| `integration-api-validator` | Characterizes an integration's API and finds the closest exemplar via parallel Explore searches. Outputs `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md`. **Read-only** — never writes against the vendor API. | Yes — re-run when a vendor's API changes or you need to refresh exemplar guidance. |

-| `integration-data-seeder` | Seeds a writes-safe vendor sandbox with enough test data for downstream validation: products, inventory, orders distributed across states, returns. # Pull requests (pokedex)

## CI test scope

Every PR body sets the CI test scope with a line `.github/workflows/ci.yml` parses, in exactly this form:

    test override: `yarn test <args>`

Set it when you open the PR, unless the default `-s` is already the right scope. Do **not** add a `<!-- auto-tests -->` marker: an unmarked override is treated as final and runs exactly those args.

- **Integration PR** (touches `integrations/{type}/{name}/` and/or `test/integrations/{type}/{name}_test.py`): `test override: ` `yarn test -k <name>`. The integration name only, nothing before `-k`. A stale-schedule or single-integration fix is always one integration; a change that reaches the framework is a non-integration PR.
- **Multi-integration sweep** (a `/fix-tests` run touching several integrations and nothing else): one `-k` per changed integration, `test override: ` `yarn test -k <a> -k <b> -k <c>`. `scripts/test.py` maps each `-k` to its test file.
- **Non-integration PR** (anything else: `utils/`, `resources/`, `celery_tasks/`, `config.py`, `lambda_handlers/`, `api.py`, `scripts/`, …): keep the default `test override: ` `yarn test -s`. With no scope arg, `scripts/test.py` hands pytest no path, so the run covers the whole `test/` tree: the integration suite **and** `api` / `celery` / `lambda` / `utils` / `transports`. Shared code is exactly what can break an integration, so that is the scope you want. Narrow it only when the blast radius is provably smaller: `nonints` when the change cannot reach integration code at all, or `-k <name>` when it reaches exactly one integration (say a `config.py` constant only it reads). Say why in the PR body.
- **No test-affecting change** (docs, markdown, config only): put `[skip-tests]` in the body.

**Why:** `-s` is the widest scope, not a fallback to avoid. It is slow and hits real or sandbox vendor APIs, and that cost is worth paying whenever a change can reach integration code. `-k <name>` trades coverage for speed on a diff confined to one integration; `nonints` does the same for a diff that cannot touch integrations. Narrowing is a claim about blast radius, so make it on purpose, not by habit.

## Ship on merge

The ship block in the PR template (between the `<!-- ship-on-merge -->` markers) is a deploy request. When a PR is merged with a stage and at least one service ticked, `ship.yml` runs for exactly those services and comments on the PR with the run, commit, request, and who merged. Ticking both stages starts two independent runs; a dev failure doesn't stop prod.

- **An untouched block ships nothing.** Agents never tick a box and can't approve or merge their own work. Leave the boxes for the person who merges.
- **Copy the block from `.github/pull_request_template.md` verbatim; never retype it.** The merge run checks ticked names against that file, so a hand-typed list breaks when a service is added.
- **Read the boxes before you merge.** Anyone with write access can tick one, and GitHub doesn't show the workflow who did. The person who merges owns the release. Prod ships are recorded, not gated.
- **Ticking `crawler` kills running crawls.** They restart only after their heartbeat goes stale (up to 10 minutes). Most resume from their saved page; a few integrations opt out and start over.

## Ship on merge

The ship block in the PR template (between the `<!-- ship-on-merge -->` markers) is a deploy request. When a PR is merged with a stage and at least one service ticked, `ship.yml` runs for exactly those services and comments on the PR with the run, commit, request, and who merged. Ticking both stages starts two independent runs; a dev failure doesn't stop prod.

- **An untouched block ships nothing.** Agents never tick a box and can't approve or merge their own work. Leave the boxes for the person who merges.

- **Read the boxes before you merge.** Anyone with write access can tick one, and GitHub doesn't show the workflow who did. The person who merges owns the release. Prod ships are recorded, not gated.
- **Ticking `crawler` kills running crawls.** They restart only after their heartbeat goes stale (up to 10 minutes). Most resume from their saved page; a few integrations opt out and start over.

# Templates — PR body + mapping comment

[`workflows/create.md`](../workflows/create.md) builds from these templates and [`workflows/refresh.md`](../workflows/refresh.md) parses and patches them. Refresh mode matches the structural anchors below character for character, and open PRs already carry them. Never change an anchor; doing so is a MAJOR version bump (see [CHANGELOG.md](../CHANGELOG.md)).

---

## Pokedex PR body

The title grammar is in [create.md step 7](../workflows/create.md#7-open-the-pr).

### Canonical section order

```markdown
## Summary
- Integration: {name} ({type})
- Source context: {Linear ticket URL / Slack thread / paste — whatever the user provided}
- Methods implemented: {list}
- Mode: new-integration | add-function
- Gotchas: {`included in this PR` if create step 5 staged a commit; `none surfaced` if file clean; omit line entirely otherwise}

## Validation status
- `yarn test -k {name}`: {N passed / M failed / K skipped}
- Live `yarn crawl` coverage: {summary — e.g. "100 orders observed, all BLOCKED state; shipped-state path unvalidated"}
- All APPROVE_WITH_NOTES advisories from per-function reviews are listed below.

## Outstanding questions (please answer before merge)
*Pull from APPROVE_WITH_NOTES verdicts, function-writer `unresolved` notes, and api-summary.md "Known gotchas / unknowns".*
- {question 1 — e.g. "Vendor sandbox can't ship orders without contacting support; should we open ticket #N or defer to first customer?"}
- {question 2}

## Recommendations (next steps after merge)
*Pull from validation gaps and reviewer advisory notes.*
- {recommendation 1 — e.g. "Seed the sandbox with 5+ SHIPPED orders to validate format_order's shipped-state path."}
- {recommendation 2}

## Field-mapping decisions
*Reference: `.claude/references/{name}/api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions" section.*
{One line per non-obvious mapping (IntegrationNotImplemented choices, .get() with rationale, mappings to non-canonical source fields), each pointing at its api-summary.md entry.}

## Sandbox limitations encountered
*What you couldn't validate live, and why.*
- {limitation 1 — e.g. "All sandbox orders in BLOCKED state due to ASN seed-data gap"}
- {limitation 2}

## Test plan
- [ ] `yarn test -k {name}` passes locally
- [ ] Filtered tests for each new method pass
- [ ] Sandbox-coverage gaps acknowledged in this description
- [ ] api-summary.md "Field-mapping decisions" section reviewed
- [ ] Logo uploaded to `s3://trackstarlogosbucket/{name}.png`

<!-- CI: edit args after "yarn test", or use [skip-tests] to skip -->
test override: `yarn test -k {name}`

{ship block, copied verbatim from between the <!-- ship-on-merge --> markers in
.github/pull_request_template.md, every box left unticked}

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

Keep every section short (the PR description ceiling in `.claude/rules/communications.md`): one line per question, recommendation, mapping decision or limitation, no paragraphs. If a section has nothing to report, keep the heading and write `- none` under it. Never drop a canonical heading.

### Structural anchors (verbatim — refresh mode parses these)

Section headings (case-sensitive, exact match):

- `## Summary`
- `## Validation status`
- `## Outstanding questions (please answer before merge)`: match the heading text up to and including `Outstanding questions`. Old PRs may not have the parenthetical.
- `## Recommendations (next steps after merge)`: same rule for the parenthetical.
- `## Field-mapping decisions`
- `## Sandbox limitations encountered`
- `## Test plan`

CI override block (after `## Test plan`, both lines verbatim):

```
<!-- CI: edit args after "yarn test", or use [skip-tests] to skip -->
test override: `yarn test -k {name}`
```

Pokedex CI finds the test command by the HTML comment, so both lines must be present. Always use this `-k {name}` override, never the repo template's default `yarn test -s`, which runs hundreds of unrelated tests (`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md` "CI test scope"). Copy the ship block from the repo template and leave every box unticked (`.claude/rules/pull-requests.md` "Ship on merge"). Refresh mode keeps this block verbatim, and appends it if it is missing.

### When source data is sparse (no api-summary.md)

The sections that come from `api-summary.md` (`Validation status`, `Outstanding questions`, `Recommendations`, `Field-mapping decisions`, `Sandbox limitations encountered`) keep their heading and get one placeholder line, so refresh mode can fill them in later:

```markdown
## Outstanding questions (please answer before merge)
_No api-summary.md available at PR creation time; populate manually or re-run `/integration-pr <pr>` after creating one._
```

`## Summary`, `## Test plan` and the CI override block always come from the branch and the template, never from `api-summary.md`.

---

## Mapping comment

Post it as a **separate PR comment**, not in the body, so the body and the comment can be edited independently. Refresh mode finds the comment by its marker line.

### Canonical shape

```markdown
<!-- trackstar-mapping-comment-v1 -->

## Field mappings — {name}

### get_products  (`format_product`)

<details>
<summary>Canonical mappings</summary>

| Canonical field | Source path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `product.sku` | |
| `name` | `product.title` | |
| `created_date` | `IntegrationNotImplemented` | |
| `updated_date` | `product.lastModifiedAt` | |
| ... | ... | |

</details>

<details>
<summary>Sample raw item from /products</summary>

```json
{ "sku": "SKU-001", "title": "Widget", ... }
```

</details>

### create_order  (body construction inlined per integration-patterns.md)

<details>
<summary>Canonical mappings (canonical → vendor payload)</summary>

| Canonical input | Source payload path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `shipping_address.line1` | `shipTo.street` | |
| `line_items[].sku` | `lines[].productCode` | |
| ... | ... | |

</details>
```

### Structural anchors (verbatim)

- **Marker line**, always the first line of the comment: `<!-- trackstar-mapping-comment-v1 -->`
- **Heading**: `## Field mappings — {name}`. The dash is an em-dash (U+2014), not a hyphen.
- **Per-method heading**: `### {method_name}  (\`format_{x}\`)`, with two spaces before the parenthetical.
- **Read-side mapping `<details>`**: `<summary>Canonical mappings</summary>` (no parenthetical).
- **Write-side mapping `<details>`**: `<summary>Canonical mappings (canonical → vendor payload)</summary>`. The arrow is `→` (U+2192).
- **Raw-sample `<details>`**: `<summary>Sample raw item from {endpoint}</summary>`, where endpoint is the path the method calls (e.g. `/products`, `/v1/orders`).

### Notes column conventions

- Empty for plain 1:1 mappings.
- Required for: `IntegrationNotImplemented` rows (why the field can't be sourced), `.get()` with a default (when the field is missing), unit conversions (e.g. minor units vs whole currency), conditional mappings, and fields taken from a less obvious source than the name suggests.
- Source: `api-summary.md` "Field-mapping decisions" first, then the code.
- Each note stands on its own. Don't point at `api-summary.md` or any other file; write the needed context into the note.

### When the sample isn't available

If [`workflows/samples.md`](../workflows/samples.md) ends at its placeholder step for a method, render the raw-sample block as:

```markdown
<details>
<summary>Sample raw item from /endpoint</summary>

_Sample not captured — neither api-summary.md, yarn curl, nor yarn crawl could provide. Capture manually and re-run `/integration-pr <pr>`._

</details>
```

The anchor stays in place so refresh mode can fill it later, and no data is faked.

entries.description: List comments on a Linear issue, project, initiative, document, project milestone, or project/initiative status update. Provide exactly one of `issueId`, `projectId`, `initiativeId`, `documentId`, `milestoneId`, or `statusUpdateId`. For issues, projects, and initiatives this returns both top-level discussion threads and inline description comments. Inline (anchored) comments carry a non-null `quotedText` set to the snippet of description text they reference. Returned comments include `author` and nullable `onBehalfOf`; when set, `onBehalfOf` identifies the user the agent author acted for. Files uploaded in comment bodies are returned in `attachments` with titles and download URLs, not issue attachment IDs. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes; call list_comments again to refresh them. Download documents using these URLs and process them with your own file tools.

issueId.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). P-prefixed identifiers (e.g., P-ENG-123) are projects, not issues (provide exactly one parent)

projectId.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

initiativeId.description: Initiative name, ID, identifier (e.g., I-123), or slug (provide exactly one parent)

documentId.description: Document ID or slug (provide exactly one parent)

milestoneId.description: Milestone UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve milestone names via `list_milestones` first.

statusUpdateId.description: Status update UUID (provide exactly one parent). Resolve status updates via `get_status_updates` first.

statusUpdateType.description: Type of status update named by `statusUpdateId`, as returned by `get_status_updates`. Only valid together with `statusUpdateId`; omit to check both project and initiative status updates.

import json
import signal
import time
from datetime import timedelta

from config import LAMBDA_SERVICES, PERMISSION_VALIDATOR_GET_TIMEOUT
from resources import function_to_resource_map
from utils.boto import get_auth_code_row, update_auth_code_column, app_decrypt
from utils.exceptions import (
    format_exception,
    PermissionsException,
    InvalidCredentialsException,
    PermissionValidationTimeout,
)
from utils.integrations import get_integration_file
from utils.lambda_util import LambdaContextManager
from utils.logutil import getLogger
from utils.utils import now

logger = getLogger()


def raise_get_timeout(signum, frame):
    raise PermissionValidationTimeout(
        f"permission validation get timed out after {PERMISSION_VALIDATOR_GET_TIMEOUT}s"
    )


def handler(event, context):
    timeout = LAMBDA_SERVICES["permission-validator"]["timeout"] - 5
    with LambdaContextManager(event, context, timeout=timeout):
        for record in event.get("Records", []):
            msg = json.loads(record["body"])
            auth_code = msg["auth_code"]
            integration_type = msg["integration_type"]
            integration_name = msg["integration_name"]
            function_name = msg["function_name"]

            logger.updateConfig(
                {
                    "integration_name": integration_name,
                    "function_name": function_name,
                }
            )

            auth_code_row = get_auth_code_row(auth_code)

            app_integration_secret = auth_code_row["integration_secret"]
            raw_integration_secret = app_decrypt(app_integration_secret)
            additional_fields = auth_code_row["additional_fields"]

            integration_file = get_integration_file(integration_name, integration_type)
            integration = integration_file.Integration(
                integration_secret=raw_integration_secret,
                auth_code=auth_code,
                connection_additional_fields=additional_fields,
            )
            resource_type = function_to_resource_map[integration_type][function_name]
            resource = resource_type(integration)
            first_loop = True
            first_crawl = False
            end_time = now()
            start_time = end_time - timedelta(hours=1)
            # copied in base_test get_with_perm_validator
            get_function = resource.get_function()

            failed_urls = []
            blocked = False
            failed_to_test = False
            timed_out = False
            # the context manager owns SIGALRM for the whole invocation, so hand it back
            outer_handler = signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, raise_get_timeout)
            outer_remaining = signal.alarm(PERMISSION_VALIDATOR_GET_TIMEOUT)
            get_started_at = time.time()
            try:
                # same setup the crawler gives the function; without it a browser
                # carrier has no session and every validation records failed_to_test
                with integration.crawl_scope(resource):
                    rsp = get_function(start_time, end_time, first_crawl, first_loop)
            except PermissionValidationTimeout as exc:
                logger.error(format_exception(exc))
                timed_out = True
                failed_to_test = True
            except (PermissionsException, InvalidCredentialsException) as exc:
                logger.error(format_exception(exc))
                blocked = True
                if isinstance(exc, InvalidCredentialsException):
                    url = "-"
                elif isinstance(exc, PermissionsException):
                    url = exc.url
                else:
                    raise Exception("improperly handled exception!")
                failed_urls.append(url)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(
                    f"Non-Connection Error in permissions validation: {format_exception(e)}"
                )
                failed_to_test = True
            else:
                api_call_errors = integration.api_call_errors
                for error in api_call_errors.values():
                    if error:
                        failed_urls.append(error.url)
            finally:
                signal.alarm(0)
                signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, outer_handler)
                if outer_remaining:
                    get_elapsed = int(time.time() - get_started_at)
                    signal.alarm(max(1, outer_remaining - get_elapsed))

            column_dict = {
                "implemented": True,
                "failed_urls": failed_urls,
                "blocked": blocked,
                "failed_to_test": failed_to_test,
                "timed_out": timed_out,
            }
            update_auth_code_column(auth_code, resource.name(), column_dict)

        return {"status": "success", "message": "permission validation completed"}

17:`transports` is also a scope, and `nonints` runs every non-integration suite (api, celery, lambda, utils, transports). With no scope, everything runs in parallel.
74:--openapi                       # the openapi test
101:| `-n <num>` | Number of parallel workers | cores, 32 for an integration run in CI, capped at the test file count when `-k` names test files |
113:1. An exact integration name (`-k deposco`) resolves to that integration's test file.
114:2. Otherwise, every test file whose name contains the value, ignoring `-` and `_`, is selected: `-k exten` picks extensiv-3pl-central, `-k ship` picks every file with "ship" in its name (shipstation, cybership, ...).
115:3. A value that matches no file name (`-k test_get_inventory`) becomes a pytest keyword filter over `test/integrations test/transports`. It matches test names, so it usually selects tests from many files.
121:Tests run serially when `-k` resolves to a single test file, or with `--pdb` or `--serial`.
123:- An integration run splits work by file (`--dist=loadfile`), because the tests in one integration's file share a connection and run in a set order.
124:- A run that touches nothing under `test/integrations` (`api`, `celery`, `lambda`, `utils`, `transports`, `nonints`) splits by test (`--dist=load`).
126:- When `-k` names test files, the worker count is capped at the number of files: `-k deposco -k shipbob` runs two workers, `-k deposco` alone runs serially. A keyword filter (step 3 above) runs at the default count with no cap.
127:- `-n` overrides the count, still capped at the file count when `-k` names test files.
132:yarn test -k shopify                    # All shopify integration tests (serial, one file)
135:yarn test -k deposco -k shipbob         # two files, two workers, no flag needed
148:**Rule:** when using `-k`, drop the scope arg. `-k` resolves to the right files on its own. Scopes (`integrations`, `api`, `celery`, `lambda`, `utils`) are for unfiltered runs over a whole tree.

content.text:
A token the permission validator refreshes now reaches the connection row, even when the exchange runs at the same time. It's pushed to PR #6166 as `e61bca051`. The lambda and API test suites pass (308 tests), and so does the new test.

**What the exchange does now** (`api.py`, after `create_connections_row`):
- It writes `connection_id` and `org_id` onto the auth code row in one update. The validator needs `org_id` because the connection's copy of the secret is encrypted with the org's key.
- It then re-reads the auth code row. If the secret changed since the exchange first read it, the new secret goes onto the connection row and the in-memory integration used for `post_install` and `safe_me`.

**What the validator does now** (`BaseIntegration.update_integration_secret`): after saving the refreshed secret to the auth code row, it re-reads the row. If the row has a `connection_id`, it writes the new secret to that connection too.

**Why both sides check:** what you described doesn't cover every timing on its own. If the exchange reads the old secret, then the validator refreshes and finds no `connection_id` yet, the connection ends up with the old secret. For integrations that issue a new refresh token each time and invalidate the old one (Squarespace), that breaks the connection. Having each side write its own value and then read the other's means at least one of them always catches it. For that to hold, `get_auth_code_row` now reads with `ConsistentRead=True`, so each side sees the other's latest write.

**Tests:**
- The new test, `test_exchange_picks_up_secret_refreshed_by_permission_validator`, forces the bad timing: a refresh lands just before the exchange writes `connection_id`. It checks that the connection ends up with the refreshed secret.
- I didn't confirm the test fails without the fix.
- No test covers the validator's side. The existing validator tests mock out the code that saves the secret, so they never reach it.

DynamoDB reads are eventually consistent by default: a read can return data from just before a write that has already finished, usually for up to about a second. `ConsistentRead=True` makes the read return every write that finished before it. It costs twice the read capacity and only works on the table itself, not on a secondary index.

That's why the fix needs it. Each side writes its own value and then reads the other's. With default reads, both reads could miss the other side's write, and the connection would keep the old token.

I posted the explanation as an inline comment on the `ConsistentRead=True` line in `utils/boto.py:1646`: https://github.com/trackstarhq/pokedex/pull/6166#discussion_r4085741831

**What it does:** DynamoDB reads are eventually consistent by default. A read can come back without a write that already finished, usually for up to about a second. `ConsistentRead=True` makes the read include every write that finished before it. It costs twice as much to read, and it only works on the table itself, not on a secondary index.

**Why this fix needs it:**
- The exchange writes `connection_id`, then reads the secret.
- The permission validator writes the secret, then reads `connection_id`.
- With default reads, both sides could miss the other's write, and the connection would keep the old token.
